Answer: C
Reason: The sequential chest X-rays demonstrate rapidly evolving, diffuse bilateral alveolar opacities (Figure 1 and 3) that show significant resolution by day 4 (Figure 4a), a pattern characteristic of Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS) responding to mechanical ventilation and supportive care. While cardiogenic edema can resolve quickly, the severity and distribution here, combined with the specific "day 4" timeline often cited in ARDS case literature regarding ventilator management, make ARDS the most likely diagnosis among the choices.
